findings.title: No robots.txt found
findings.evidence: robots_txt.found is false — no /robots.txt served. Crawlers fall back to default behaviour, and the site has no stated policy on AI access.

suggested_action.summary: Add a robots.txt that explicitly states which crawlers may access the site. Silence is ambiguous; an explicit allow is not.

findings.title: Render-gap check did not run — JavaScript dependency unverified
findings.evidence: render_check.status = 'skipped'. Reason: no eligible pages to render

suggested_action.summary: Install the headless browser and re-run to confirm whether content is JavaScript-dependent.
suggested_action.detail: Run: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium. Note that `pip install playwright` alone does not download the browser binary; the second command is required. Until this check runs, no conclusion either way can be drawn about JS-dependent content.

suggested_actions.title: Publish an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt
suggested_actions.rationale: No sitemap was found via robots.txt or at /sitemap.xml. Without one, a crawler can only reach pages that happen to be linked from pages it already has, so anything more than two clicks from the homepage may never be discovered.

suggested_actions.title: Publish an llms.txt orientation file
suggested_actions.rationale: No /llms.txt was found. The file is a short, machine-readable index pointing crawlers at the canonical pages for the brand rather than making them infer structure from navigation. Adoption is still emerging, but the cost is a single static file.

suggested_actions.title: Add a changelog or insights section that updates on a real cadence
suggested_actions.rationale: No dateModified or datePublished appears in any structured data block, and no blog, news or changelog section exists among the pages found. Nothing signals that the site is actively maintained. A genuinely-updated page is the honest way to create that signal — padding dateModified on static pages is detectable and counterproductive. Coverage: all 0 internal links from the homepage were crawled.

suggested_actions.title: Add a comparison or alternatives page
suggested_actions.rationale: No comparison, versus or alternatives page was found. Comparison queries are among the highest-volume prompts assistants receive. When a brand does not publish its own comparison, assistants fall back to third-party review sites and competitor pages — which get cited instead, and frame the comparison unfavourably. Coverage: all 0 internal links from the homepage were crawled.

suggested_actions.title: Publish case studies or a named-clients page
suggested_actions.rationale: No case-study, customer or portfolio page was found. Named engagements are the most reusable corroboration a B2B site can create: they give other sites something specific to reference, and they answer "who actually uses this" — a question assistants are asked constantly and currently cannot answer from this domain. Coverage: all 0 internal links from the homepage were crawled.
